parts.title: Orientation
parts.summary: What Turkish is, the idea that runs through its grammar (one meaning per suffix, in a fixed order, shaped by vowel harmony), and how this guide works.

parts.title: Sounds and script
parts.summary: Eight vowels and the three questions that classify them, the consonants, soft g and long vowels, two-way and four-way harmony, consonant alternations and buffer letters, stress, and the spelling of loanwords and names.

parts.title: The simplest sentences
parts.summary: Saying what something is, personal endings, plurals, negation with değil, yes-no questions with mI, existence with var and yok, basic word order, and the first verb form.

parts.title: Nouns and their machinery
parts.summary: The cases, possessive suffixes and the genitive, pronominal n, noun compounds, 'having', pronouns, demonstratives, question words, -(y)lA and the -ki suffix.

parts.title: Verbs: the core system
parts.summary: The slot order of the verb, imperatives, the past in -DI, the future, the aorist, the evidential -mIş, the copular markers, compound tenses, -DIr, necessity, ability, the optative, questions on verbs, olmak, and choosing a tense.

parts.title: Modifying and linking
parts.summary: Adjectives and adverbs, comparison, numbers and time, postpositions and location nouns, conjunctions and particles, derivational suffixes and reduplication.

parts.title: Complex sentences
parts.summary: Subordination by nominalisation: -mAk, -mA, -DIK and -(y)AcAK clauses, participles and relative clauses, converbs, time, reason and purpose clauses, conditionals, reported speech, indefinites and concession.

parts.title: Advanced and special topics
parts.summary: Passive, causative and stacked voice, reflexive and reciprocal, evidentiality and mirativity in depth, compound verbs, politeness, formal and colloquial registers, focus and word order, the Ottoman legacy, and the Turkic family.

parts.title: Reading real texts
parts.summary: Eight graded passages: proverbs, two Nasreddin Hoca anecdotes, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Turkish Wikipedia on Istanbul, Ömer Seyfettin's Kaşağı, Atatürk's Address to the Youth, and a capstone poem by Yunus Emre.

parts.title: Reference
parts.summary: The suffix order chart, noun and verb tables, core vocabulary, glossary of terms and abbreviations, annotated bibliography.

lessons.title: What Turkish is
lessons.point: Place Turkish in time, space and family, and know which Turkish this guide teaches

lessons.title: The organising idea: one meaning per suffix, in a fixed order
lessons.point: See how a long Turkish word is built from small suffixes in a fixed order, each shaped by vowel harmony

lessons.title: How to use this guide
lessons.point: Read the glosses, the suffix notation in capitals and the confidence dots, and know where the facts come from

lessons.title: Eight vowels and three questions
lessons.point: Pronounce the eight vowels and sort each by front or back, rounded or not, high or low

lessons.title: The consonants and their letters
lessons.point: Pronounce c, ç, ş, j, r and the front and back versions of k, g and l

lessons.title: Soft g, long vowels and the circumflex
lessons.point: Read ğ, which lengthens or links vowels, and the circumflex on â, î, û in loanwords

lessons.title: Two-way harmony: e or a
lessons.point: Choose between e and a in a suffix by looking at the last vowel of the word

lessons.title: Four-way harmony: i, ı, u or ü
lessons.point: Choose among i, ı, u and ü in a suffix, and read the capital-letter notation -lAr, -(y)I used in this guide

lessons.title: Consonants that change at the joins
lessons.point: Predict d or t at the start of a suffix, k to ğ and p to b at the end of a stem, and the buffer letters y, n and s

lessons.title: Stress and intonation
lessons.point: Put the stress on the last syllable by default, and know the suffixes and words that move it

lessons.title: Loanwords, names and spelling
lessons.point: Handle loanwords that break harmony, the apostrophe before suffixes on names, and the 1928 alphabet

lessons.title: This is a book: sentences without a verb
lessons.point: Say what something is with no verb and no 'the', using bir for 'a'

lessons.title: I am a teacher: personal endings
lessons.point: Add the endings that say who is something: -(y)Im, -sIn, -(y)Iz, -sInIz, -lAr

lessons.title: More than one: the plural -lAr
lessons.point: Make nouns plural and know when Turkish leaves the plural out

lessons.title: Not: değil
lessons.point: Deny that something is something with değil and its personal endings

lessons.title: Yes-no questions with mI
lessons.point: Ask a yes-no question with the particle mI and place it on the word in question

lessons.title: There is and there is not: var, yok and the locative
lessons.point: Say that something exists or is somewhere, with var, yok and -DA 'in, at'

lessons.title: Word order: subject, object, verb
lessons.point: Put the verb last and the most important new word just before it

lessons.title: The first verb form: -(I)yor
lessons.point: Say what someone is doing now, with the stem, -(I)yor and the personal endings

lessons.title: Not doing: the negative -mA and questions on verbs
lessons.point: Make verbs negative with -mA and ask questions with mI after -(I)yor

lessons.title: The accusative: the definite object
lessons.point: Mark a specific object with -(y)I and leave a non-specific one bare

lessons.title: The dative: to and towards
lessons.point: Mark where something goes and to whom with -(y)A

lessons.title: The ablative: from and through
lessons.point: Mark where something comes from with -DAn, and know its other uses

lessons.title: Possessive suffixes: my house, your house
lessons.point: Add -(I)m, -(I)n, -(s)I, -(I)mIz, -(I)nIz, -lArI to a noun

lessons.title: The genitive: the possessor
lessons.point: Build 'Ali's house' as Ali'nin evi, with the genitive on the possessor and a possessive on the thing owned

lessons.title: Cases after a possessive: the buffer n
lessons.point: Put case endings after a third-person possessive, with the n that appears there

lessons.title: Noun compounds: Türk kahvesi
lessons.point: Build compounds with the compound marker -(s)I and see how they differ from genitive phrases

lessons.title: Having: benim arabam var
lessons.point: Say what someone has with the possessive and var or yok

lessons.title: Personal pronouns and their cases
lessons.point: Use ben, sen, o, biz, siz, onlar in every case, including bana and sana, and know when to leave them out

lessons.title: This, that and the other: bu, şu, o
lessons.point: Point with bu, şu and o, and use burada, şurada, orada

lessons.title: Question words
lessons.point: Ask who, what, where, when, how and why, keeping the question word in place

lessons.title: With: -(y)lA
lessons.point: Say 'with' and 'by means of' with ile and its suffixed form -(y)lA

lessons.title: The one in the house: -ki
lessons.point: Turn a place, a time or a possessor into a word that describes or stands for a thing, with -ki

lessons.title: The verb template: slots in a fixed order
lessons.point: See the order of the slots in a verb (stem, voice, negation, ability, tense, copula, person) and why they cannot be shuffled

lessons.title: Commands: the bare stem and its relatives
lessons.point: Give orders with the bare stem, -(y)In, -(y)InIz and -sIn, and forbid with -mA

lessons.title: The past: -DI
lessons.point: Say what happened with -DI and its own set of personal endings

lessons.title: The future: -(y)AcAK
lessons.point: Say what will happen with -(y)AcAK, including its spoken shortenings

lessons.title: The aorist: how it is built
lessons.point: Form the aorist in -r, -Ar or -Ir, including the thirteen stems that take -Ir

lessons.title: The aorist: what it means, and its negative -mAz
lessons.point: Use the aorist for habits, general truths, offers and promises, and form its negative

lessons.title: The evidential past: -mIş
lessons.point: Report something you did not witness or have just realised, and contrast it with -DI

lessons.title: Was, apparently is, if it is: -(y)DI, -(y)mIş, -(y)sA on nouns
lessons.point: Add past, evidential and conditional markers to nouns and adjectives

lessons.title: Compound tenses: geliyordu, gelirdi, gelmişti
lessons.point: Stack a copular marker on a tense to say 'was doing', 'used to do', 'had done'

lessons.title: The -DIr ending: is, must be
lessons.point: Use -DIr for formal statements and for 'it must be so'

lessons.title: Must: -mAlI
lessons.point: Say what must or should be done with -mAlI

lessons.title: Can and cannot: -(y)Abil and -(y)AmA
lessons.point: Say what someone can do with -(y)Abil and cannot do with -(y)AmA

lessons.title: Let me, let's: the optative
lessons.point: Make suggestions and first-person requests with -(y)AyIm and -(y)AlIm

lessons.title: Where mI goes in each tense
lessons.point: Place the question particle correctly after -DI, before the person ending elsewhere

lessons.title: Olmak: to be and to become
lessons.point: Use olmak where the copula has no form: future, infinitive, 'become'

lessons.title: Choosing a tense
lessons.point: Choose between -(I)yor, the aorist, -DI, -mIş and -(y)AcAK by what you mean

lessons.title: Adjectives and adverbs
lessons.point: Use adjectives before nouns and as nouns, and make adverbs from them

lessons.title: Comparison: daha and en
lessons.point: Compare with -DAn daha and pick out the most with en

lessons.title: Numbers, ordinals and distributives
lessons.point: Count, order (birinci) and share out (birer, ikişer), with nouns left singular

lessons.title: Time, days and dates
lessons.point: Tell the time, give dates and say how long ago and how long for

lessons.title: Postpositions with the bare noun: için, gibi, kadar
lessons.point: Use the postpositions that follow a bare noun or a genitive pronoun

lessons.title: Postpositions with the dative and ablative
lessons.point: Use göre, doğru, kadar, karşı with the dative and önce, sonra, beri with the ablative

lessons.title: On, under, in front: location nouns
lessons.point: Say where things are with üst, alt, ön, arka, iç, yan and a case ending

lessons.title: Conjunctions and particles: ve, ama, de, ya da
lessons.point: Join words and sentences with ve, ama, fakat, ya da, hem...hem, ne...ne and the particle de

lessons.title: Making words: -lI, -sIz, -lIK, -CI
lessons.point: Build new nouns and adjectives with the common derivational suffixes

lessons.title: Making verbs: -lA, -lAş, -lAn
lessons.point: Turn nouns and adjectives into verbs, and verbs into nouns with -(y)Iş and -mA

lessons.title: Doubling: yavaş yavaş, masmavi, kitap mitap
lessons.point: Use the three kinds of reduplication for manner, intensity and 'and so on'

lessons.title: Clauses as nouns 1: the infinitive -mAk
lessons.point: Say 'I want to go' and 'going is hard' with -mAk

lessons.title: Clauses as nouns 2: -mA with a possessive
lessons.point: Say 'I want you to go' with -mA plus a possessive ending

lessons.title: Clauses as nouns 3: -DIK and -(y)AcAK for facts
lessons.point: Say 'I know that you came' and 'I know that you will come'

lessons.title: Relative clauses 1: -(y)An
lessons.point: Describe a noun by what it does, and use -(y)An forms as nouns ('those who came')

lessons.title: Relative clauses 2: -DIK and -(y)AcAK with a possessive
lessons.point: Describe a noun by what someone else does to it or where it happens

lessons.title: Linking actions: -(y)Ip and -(y)ArAk
lessons.point: Chain actions with -(y)Ip and say how something is done with -(y)ArAk

lessons.title: When, while, before, after
lessons.point: Build time clauses with -(y)IncA, -ken, -DIğI zaman, -mAdAn önce, -DIktAn sonra

lessons.title: Because and in order to
lessons.point: Give reasons with -DIğI için and purposes with -mAk için and diye

lessons.title: If: the conditional -sA
lessons.point: Make real conditions with -(y)sA after a tense, and with eğer

lessons.title: If only: unreal conditions and wishes
lessons.point: Say what would have happened, and wish with keşke

lessons.title: Reported speech: demek, diye and ki
lessons.point: Report what people said, with quotation, diye and the Persian-style ki

lessons.title: Someone, no one, anything: indefinites and hiç
lessons.point: Use biri, bir şey, hiç kimse, hiçbir şey with a negative verb

lessons.title: Although and even if
lessons.point: Concede with -sA da, -DIğI halde and -mAsInA rağmen

lessons.title: Putting clauses together
lessons.point: Take apart and build long sentences with several nominalised clauses, the order of the suffixes guiding you

lessons.title: The passive: -Il and -In
lessons.point: Form and use the passive, including the impersonal passive of intransitive verbs

lessons.title: The causative: making someone do
lessons.point: Form causatives with -DIr, -t and the irregular ones, and mark the causee

lessons.title: Stacking voice suffixes
lessons.point: Read and build verbs with causative on causative and causative plus passive

lessons.title: Reflexive, reciprocal and kendi
lessons.point: Use -(I)n for actions on oneself, -(I)ş for actions on each other, and the pronoun kendi

lessons.title: Evidentiality and surprise in depth
lessons.point: Use -mIş for hearsay, inference and surprise, and in storytelling

lessons.title: Compound verbs: -(y)Iver, -(y)Adur and noun + etmek
lessons.point: Use the quick, continuous and auxiliary verb combinations

lessons.title: Politeness and address
lessons.point: Choose siz or sen, use Bey, Hanım and efendim, and make polite requests

lessons.title: The formal written register
lessons.point: Read -mAktA, -DIr, -mAksIzIn and the long nominal sentences of news and official prose

lessons.title: Everyday speech: gelicem, napıyosun
lessons.point: Recognise the spoken reductions of -(I)yor and -(y)AcAK and other informal forms

lessons.title: Focus, topic and words after the verb
lessons.point: Move words for emphasis, and use the slot after the verb for afterthoughts

lessons.title: The Ottoman legacy: Arabic and Persian layers
lessons.point: Recognise Arabic and Persian loanwords, the izafet, and the results of the language reform

lessons.title: Turkish and the Turkic family
lessons.point: Place Turkish among Azerbaijani, Turkmen, Uzbek, Kazakh and the rest, and among its own dialects

lessons.title: Reading 1: Proverbs
lessons.point: Read eight Turkish proverbs, each a full sentence with the aorist, -(y)An and converbs

lessons.title: Reading 2: Nasreddin Hoca, The quilt is gone, the fight is over
lessons.point: Read a short anecdote told in -mIş, with its punch line in -DI

lessons.title: Reading 3: Nasreddin Hoca, God's guest
lessons.point: Read an anecdote told in the aorist present with dialogue

lessons.title: Reading 4: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Articles 1 to 3
lessons.point: Read formal legal prose with necessitatives, passives and Ottoman vocabulary

lessons.title: Reading 5: Istanbul, from Turkish Wikipedia
lessons.point: Read modern expository prose with participles and -mAktA

lessons.title: Reading 6: Ömer Seyfettin, The Currycomb
lessons.point: Read the opening of a classic short story told with -IrdI and -Iyordu

lessons.title: Reading 7: Atatürk, Address to the Youth
lessons.point: Read a famous speech of 1927 and see how much of its vocabulary has since been replaced

lessons.title: Reading 8 (capstone): Yunus Emre, 'Your love has taken me from myself'
lessons.point: Read a medieval poem in Old Anatolian Turkish, with its older endings explained

lessons.title: The suffix order chart
lessons.point: See every noun and verb suffix in its slot, with its harmony pattern and gloss

lessons.title: Noun and pronoun tables
lessons.point: Look up case and possessive forms for every stem type and the pronouns

lessons.title: Verb tables
lessons.point: Look up every tense, mood and non-finite form of model verbs

lessons.title: Core vocabulary
lessons.point: Find every word taught in the guide with the lesson that introduces it

lessons.title: Glossary of terms and abbreviations
lessons.point: Look up every grammatical term and gloss abbreviation

lessons.title: Annotated bibliography
lessons.point: Know which grammars, dictionaries and corpora to use next
